title: Laksa
subtitle: Malaysian coconut curry noodle soup
excerpt: The great noodle soup of Malaysia and Singapore: thick rice noodles in a fragrant, fiery coconut milk broth built on a spice paste of shrimp paste, lemongrass, and chilli, topped with prawns, tofu, and fresh garnishes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Laksa is the definitive noodle soup of the Peranakan (Straits Chinese) culinary tradition, found across Malaysia, Singapore, and Indonesia with significant regional variations. The two main types are curry laksa (with a rich, coconut milk-based broth) and asam laksa (a sour, tamarind-based broth without coconut). Curry laksa, the version here, is the most widely eaten outside Southeast Asia: a broth made from a ground spice paste of shrimp paste, lemongrass, galangal, dried chillies, and turmeric, cooked in oil until fragrant, then enriched with coconut milk and chicken or prawn stock. The Penang laksa (asam laksa) is separately celebrated, with a sour, fish-based broth. The version here is a practical interpretation of curry laksa that uses accessible ingredients.

content.text: Fry the spice paste in oil for a full 5 to 8 minutes until it is dark and fragrant and the oil has separated from the paste; undercooked spice paste produces a raw, harsh flavour. The coconut milk goes in after the paste is properly cooked; add it gradually to prevent splitting.

content.text: Make the spice paste: blend the lemongrass, ginger, garlic, chilli, shrimp paste, turmeric, and coriander with 3 tablespoons of water to a smooth paste. Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Fry the paste, stirring constantly, for 6 to 8 minutes until very fragrant and the oil has separated.

Add the stock and bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes. Add the coconut milk and bring back to a gentle simmer. Season with fish sauce and lime juice. Add the prawns and tofu. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until the prawns are pink and cooked through.
Divide the cooked noodles between 4 deep bowls. Ladle the broth, prawns, and tofu over. Top with beansprouts, coriander, and spring onions. Serve with lime wedges.
